slides.title: Problem-Solving Strategy
text: Read carefully — identify what is given and what is asked
Draw a diagram — label all known sides and angles
Identify the right triangle(s) in the problem
Choose the trig ratio: SOH CAH TOA
Set up the equation and solve for the unknown
Check — does the answer make sense? Include units.

slides.title: Finding a Side Length with Trig
text: Hypotenuse = 20 m, angle = 42°. Find the opposite side.
Know: hypotenuse = 20, angle = 42°. Need: opposite side → use sin (SOH)

slides.title: Word Problem — One Right Triangle
text: A 20 ft ladder leans against a wall at 65° from the ground. How high up the wall does it reach?
Hyp = 20 ft, angle = 65°, find opposite (wall height) → use sin (SOH)

slides.title: Finding an Angle Using Inverse Trig
text: Use sin⁻¹ (arcsin), cos⁻¹, or tan⁻¹ to find angles.
⚠ Calculator must be in DEGREE mode when using inverse trig!

slides.title: Angles of Elevation and Depression
text: Both measured from the horizontal (never from vertical)
Angle of elevation = angle of depression (alternate interior angles)
Always draw the horizontal at the observer's eye level.

slides.title: Example — Angle of Depression
text: From a 120 ft lighthouse top, depression to a ship is 15°. Find the distance.
Depression from top = elevation from ship = 15°

slides.title: Trig Functions and d = rt
text: d = rt combined with trig lets us resolve motion into horizontal and vertical components.

slides.title: Example — Trig and d = rt
text: A plane flies at 250 mph, 30° north of east, for 2 hours. How far N and E?

slides.title: Solving a Right Triangle
text: "Solve" a triangle: Find all 3 sides and all 3 angles. You need at least one side plus one other known part.
Third angle: A + B = 90° → B = 90° − A
Use trig ratios to find unknown sides

slides.title: Example — Solving a Right Triangle
text: Given: A = 35°, c = 24 (hypotenuse), C = 90°. Find B, a, and b.

slides.title: Word Problem — Two Right Triangles
text: Elevation to a building top is 31° from one point, 53° from 50 ft closer. Find the height.

slides.title: You Try
text: A surveyor stands 80 ft from a building. The angle of elevation to the roof is 42°. Find the building height.
